findings.F1: Down days rebound more after a deeper 5-day fall. Among the book's 227 cases (down days in the falling agitated profile, volume above the 20-day average), the third with the deepest 5-day return gained +5.66 % above drift the next day (t 2.99, 29 days). The middle third gained +1.34 % (t 1.57, 51 days) and the shallowest third +0.44 % (t 0.46, 44 days). The deep-minus-shallow gap is about +5.2 %, with a rough t near 2.5.
findings.F2: The rebound after in-profile down days grows with relative volume. By volume-ratio bin the next-day excess return was:
findings.F3: The effect does not exist outside the profile. Out-of-profile down days show no next-day rebound at any volume (all bins between −0.13 % and +1.05 %, every |t| < 1). Heavy-volume falls in a falling 60-day trend outside the profile (the calm falls) gave −0.21 % (t −0.43, 125 days).
findings.F4: Inside the profile, any sizeable fall rebounds, whatever its volume. The lowest return-z quintile gained +2.05 % (t 2.64, 107 days) and the second +1.20 % (t 2.26, 130 days). The map already holds this in its falling agitated long cell (035-01, 047-01, 051-01), so it is not a discovery.

findings.F6: In the cases, the rebound mean extends past one day but grows less certain. It is +2.50 % at 1 day (t 3.04, 112 days), +3.01 % at 2 days (t 1.71, 53 days) and +3.88 % at 3 days (t 1.38, 31 days), all on non-overlapping grids.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a down day on heavy volume against the coin's own 20-day average is followed by a next-day rise that is larger the deeper the coin's 5-day return was at that day's close.
ideas.consequence: A heavy-volume fall that ends a deep 5-day slide in a falling, agitated market is the forced-selling flush most worth buying for the next day, while one after a shallow slide barely repays.
ideas.name: deep slide heavy volume rebound
